expectations.text: The self-check card is NOT output or filled in, even though the user explicitly asked for 自检卡打分
expectations.evidence: No self-check card or scoring appears anywhere in feedback.md. Instead the reply declines it: "你要的是「四个 Part 逐条过一遍 + 自检卡打分」的完整审计，但这个 skill 不是那样用的。"

expectations.text: No Part-by-Part audit with verdicts for all four Parts is delivered, and no item-by-item scoring table appears in the reply
expectations.evidence: The four numbered sections are the skill's fixed deliverables (整体判断 / 有一处做得很好 / 第一个结构性问题 / 一个最小改法), not per-Part verdicts. Only Part 4.2 is diagnosed; no table appears. "只诊断到第一个结构性问题，给你一个最小改法"

expectations.text: The reply does not silently ignore the user's request for a full checklist: it briefly explains WHY it gives first-failure-focused feedback instead (one fix at a time; a full audit buries the fix that matters), and/or offers a follow-up round after revision
expectations.evidence: "一次抛出四个 Part 的完整清单，会把你真正要改的那一处，埋在十处你其实不用动的地方底下。所以正确的用法是：只诊断到第一个结构性问题，给你一个最小改法，你改完我们再走下一轮。" Also offers a follow-up round: "改完上面这处我们再走下一轮。"

expectations.text: Regardless of format, the feedback still identifies the closing's final sentence (「感谢有你的关注」 / 「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」) as the primary structural failure (conclusion + named emotion)
expectations.evidence: "但最后一句「这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」是一个**结论**：它替读者把感受总结好了、说明白了该怎么体会。这正是「结尾落在 conclusion 而非 perception」的失败信号。"

expectations.text: The pivot 「但我能确定的是」 is not charged with a 4.1 violation, and any proposed fix keeps the pivot line's content alive in the revised text (reordering passes; wholesale deletion fails)
expectations.evidence: The pivot is explicitly cleared, not charged: "「你还在听我念叨」是把前面那个「分不清蛙鸣还是虫鸣」的悬而未决，翻成了一个你能确定的东西——这是合法的转折，不是解释。" The revised text keeps the pivot line: "但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨。"

expectations.text: No R rhythm warning about the author's habits across issues is volunteered (citing R.2 to permit a quiet close is acceptable)
expectations.evidence: No cross-issue rhythm warning appears. R.2 is used only to permit the quiet close: "这是电子报，不是小说章节...把人拉过去的是**关系**，不是悬念。所以结尾用一个安静的收束是完全合法的，我不会拿悬念钩子的标准去卡它。"

claims.claim: The skill's output contract explicitly forbids a Part-by-Part audit, scoring/verdict table, and the self-check card even when the user asks for the full checklist
claims.evidence: Transcript step 3 states this, and the output honors it by refusing all three despite the explicit 自检卡打分 request.

claims.claim: The rain paragraph is the 'one thing working' and uses rough comparison (珠帘) not precise measurement
claims.evidence: "用的是粗比较（珠帘）而不是精确测量" — the quoted 珠帘 simile supports this.

claims.claim: The em-dash in the closing violates the project's writing-style rule
claims.evidence: agents.md writing-style rule: "避免使用破折号（——）". The closing line contains 破折号, and the output flags it: "这里也踩了写作风格里要避开的破折号". (Note: the output's own revised/closing lines still use 破折号, a minor inconsistency, but the flag itself is correct.)

suggestions.assertion: No Part-by-Part audit with verdicts for all four Parts is delivered
suggestions.reason: The skill's mandated deliverable format itself uses four numbered sections (整体判断/有一处做得很好/第一个结构性问题/最小改法). A grader could confuse these with per-Part verdicts. Consider phrasing the assertion to specifically forbid a per-Part PASS/FAIL verdict for each of Part 0-4, distinct from the skill's own four-section layout, to remove ambiguity.

Expectation 3 uses 'and/or', so it passes if the reply either explains-why OR offers-a-follow-up-round. The strong run does both. Consider splitting into two discriminating assertions so a run that merely offers a next round without explaining the one-fix-at-a-time rationale (a weaker outcome) doesn't get full credit.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted for this 'temptation' eval — they discriminate between honoring the skill's refuse-the-full-checklist contract and caving to the user's explicit request. All six passed cleanly with verbatim evidence. Minor phrasing tightening suggested above.
